name: Minecraft
desc: The heart and story of the game

name: Stone Age
desc: Mine Stone with your new Pickaxe

name: Getting an Upgrade
desc: Construct a better Pickaxe

name: Acquire Hardware
desc: Smelt an Iron Ingot
howToGet: Mine iron ore with a stone pickaxe or better: look for it in mountains around Y=232 or deep underground around Y=16.
Smelt the raw iron in a furnace or blast furnace: 1 raw iron plus fuel gives 1 iron ingot.
Pick the ingot up. Having one in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: A blast furnace smelts twice as fast, and a Fortune pickaxe increases the raw iron each ore drops. Iron ingots also come from village and shipwreck chests, and iron golems drop 3-5 when killed.

name: Suit Up
desc: Protect yourself with a piece of iron armor
howToGet: Mine iron ore: it generates at almost every height, with extra ore in mountain peaks around Y=232 and a second rich band deep underground around Y=16. A stone pickaxe or better is enough.
Smelt the raw iron in a furnace or blast furnace into iron ingots. A full set costs 24 ingots; boots are the cheapest piece at 4.
Craft any piece of iron armor at a crafting table.
Pick the piece up: the advancement triggers the moment any iron armor piece sits in your inventory. You don't even have to wear it.
tips: Armorer villagers sell iron armor for emeralds, village armorer chests can contain iron pieces, and zombies or skeletons occasionally drop them. Any way of getting one into your inventory counts.

name: Hot Stuff
desc: Fill a Bucket with lava
howToGet: Craft a bucket from 3 iron ingots in a V shape.
Find lava: surface lava pools, lava aquifers in deep caves, or anywhere in the Nether.
Use the bucket on a lava SOURCE block: the still blocks, not the flowing ones. Flowing lava can't be collected.
The lava bucket in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: A lava bucket smelts 100 items, the best furnace fuel in the game. Lava is even renewable: a cauldron under pointed dripstone with lava above it slowly fills with fresh lava.

name: Isn't It Iron Pick?
desc: Upgrade your Pickaxe

name: Not Today, Thank You
desc: Deflect a projectile with a Shield
howToGet: Craft a shield: 6 planks of any wood and 1 iron ingot in a Y shape.
Hold the shield in either hand and hold right-click (use) to raise it.
Face a skeleton, drowned with trident or any mob firing projectiles and let one hit your raised shield.
Blocking any projectile completes the advancement.
tips: The shield blocks all frontal projectile damage and softens melee hits, but watch out for axes: a hit from one disables your shield for 5 seconds. Arrows from Piercing crossbows also go straight through it.

name: Ice Bucket Challenge
desc: Obtain a block of Obsidian
howToGet: Get a diamond pickaxe (or netherite): obsidian can't be collected with anything weaker.
Find lava: surface lava pools, the lava aquifers deep underground, or the Nether if you're already there.
Pour water from a bucket onto a lava SOURCE block: the source turns into obsidian. Flowing lava turns into cobblestone instead, so always target the still blocks.
Mine the obsidian with the diamond pickaxe (about 9.4 seconds per block) and pick it up. Having it in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: No diamonds yet? Obsidian also generates in ruined portals and their chests, in bastion remnant chests, in village weaponsmith chests, and piglin bartering can hand it over. You only need one block.

name: Diamonds!
desc: Acquire diamonds
howToGet: Go deep: diamond ore generates in the deepslate layers, and the sweet spot is Y=-59, just above the bedrock floor.
Bring an iron pickaxe or better. Stone and wood break the ore without dropping anything.
Branch mine at Y=-59 or explore the huge caves that open down there, and mine the diamond ore you find.
Pick the diamonds up: the moment one sits in your inventory, the advancement completes.
tips: A Fortune III pickaxe more than doubles the yield of each ore, so enchant before mining a big vein. Diamonds also show up in chests in villages, shipwrecks, buried treasure, bastion remnants and end cities, and a water bucket is essential insurance against the lava lakes at that depth.

name: We Need to Go Deeper
desc: Build, light and enter a Nether Portal
howToGet: Build a nether portal frame: an upright obsidian rectangle at least 4 blocks wide and 5 tall on the outside. That takes 14 blocks, or just 10 if you leave the corners empty.
Light it: flint and steel is the standard way, but a fire charge or even fire spreading from lava and wood works too.
Step into the purple portal blocks and stand still for a few seconds.
When you arrive in the Nether, the advancement completes.
tips: Ruined portals in the Overworld can be repaired: their own chests often hold obsidian, a flint and steel, or even gold. Always carry a spare flint and steel in the Nether, because a ghast fireball can shut your portal down.

name: Cover Me with Diamonds
desc: Diamond armor saves lives
howToGet: Mine diamonds: branch mine or cave at Y=-59 (just above the bedrock layer) in the deepslate layers, where diamond ore is most common. Bring an iron pickaxe or better.
Find 4 or more diamonds. Boots are the cheapest piece (4 diamonds); a helmet costs 5, leggings 7 and a chestplate 8.
Craft the piece at a crafting table and equip it in your armor slot.
tips: A Fortune III pickaxe more than doubles your diamond yield, so enchant before mining a big vein. Diamonds also appear in chests in villages (weaponsmith), shipwrecks, buried treasure, bastions and End cities if mining is slow.

name: Enchanter
desc: Enchant an item at an Enchanting Table
howToGet: Craft an enchanting table with 4 obsidian, 2 diamonds and 1 book (a book is 3 paper + 1 leather).
Mine or gather lapis lazuli: every enchantment costs 1-3 lapis plus experience levels.
Open the table, place any enchantable item (sword, pickaxe, armor piece, book...) in the left slot and lapis in the right.
Choose any of the three offered enchantments. Your first enchant completes the advancement.
tips: Surround the table with 15 bookshelves, leaving one block of air between them and the table, to unlock level-30 enchantments. Enchanting a book stores the enchantment so you can apply it later on an anvil.

name: Zombie Doctor
desc: Weaken and then cure a Zombie Villager
howToGet: Find a zombie villager: about 5% of zombies that spawn naturally are zombie villagers. You can also let a zombie kill a villager (100% conversion on Hard, 50% on Normal, 0% on Easy).
Trap it safely: push it into a boat or a closed, roofed space so it cannot burn in daylight or escape, and so other mobs cannot interrupt.
Hit it with a Splash Potion of Weakness (brewed with a Fermented Spider Eye and a Water Bottle, no blaze powder needed). The villager should show the Weakness swirls.
Right-click it with a regular Golden Apple (not an enchanted one). You will hear a loud sound and red particles appear.
Wait 3 to 5 minutes. Placing iron bars and a bed within a 9x9x9 area around it shortens the wait.
tips: Cured villagers give you permanent trade discounts, and curing the same villager repeatedly stacks the discounts up to the maximum. This pairs perfectly with Hero of the Village for the cheapest trades in the game.

name: Eye Spy
desc: Follow an Eye of Ender
howToGet: Craft Eyes of Ender: combine Blaze Powder (from Blaze Rods farmed at a Nether fortress) with Ender Pearls (from Endermen, Piglin bartering or cleric trades). Craft at least 12.
Throw an Eye of Ender and walk in the direction it flies. It has a 20% chance to shatter per throw, so throw sparingly: walk several hundred blocks between throws.
When the eye dives into the ground, the stronghold is below. Dig down carefully (never straight down: use a staircase).
The advancement triggers the moment you enter the stronghold's bounding box.
tips: You can triangulate the stronghold with two throws from far apart: note the direction each eye flies and find where the lines cross. Bring spare eyes for the End portal itself (up to 12 more).

name: The End?
desc: Enter the End Portal

name: Nether
desc: Bring summer clothes

name: Return to Sender
desc: Destroy a Ghast with a fireball
howToGet: Find a ghast: they spawn in nether wastes, soul sand valleys and basalt deltas.

Wait for it to shoot a fireball at you, then hit the fireball back with any melee attack, or shoot it with an arrow or another projectile. The reflected fireball flies back in the direction you are aiming.
Kill the ghast with its own reflected fireball. A reflected fireball that connects kills a ghast in a single hit, so this is about aim, not damage.
The advancement (and 50 XP) is yours the moment the ghast dies to its own shot.
tips: Swing just before the fireball reaches you and keep clear line of sight. The open nether wastes are the easiest arena: no terrain for the ghast to hide behind, and you can see the shot coming from far away.

name: Those Were the Days
desc: Enter a Bastion Remnant
howToGet: Travel to the Nether and explore any biome except Basalt Deltas: Bastion Remnants never generate there. They are huge blackstone structures, visible from far away.
Equip at least one piece of gold armor before approaching: Piglins attack players without gold on sight.
Walk inside the bastion's bounding box: the advancement triggers on entry.
tips: There are four bastion types (bridge, hoglin stables, housing units and treasure room). The treasure room type has the best loot, including a chance of Netherite Upgrade smithing templates, but also the most Piglin Brutes, which are always hostile regardless of gold armor.

name: Hidden in the Depths
desc: Obtain Ancient Debris
howToGet: Ancient debris only generates in the Nether, most commonly around Y=15. Bring a diamond pickaxe or better - nothing weaker will drop it.
Dig a main tunnel at Y=15 in any Nether biome (warped forest is the safest) and branch mine every 2 blocks.
Faster method: beds. Ancient debris is blast resistant, beds are not. Place a bed 4 blocks away, stand behind a block, click it to explode, and repeat down the tunnel. TNT works the same way.
Expect roughly 1-2 debris per chunk. For a full netherite set (36 ingots with the smithing template upgrades) you need 36 debris plus the template from bastions.
Smelt each debris into netherite scrap; 4 scrap + 4 gold ingots make one netherite ingot.
tips: Beds explode in the Nether - always place a solid block between you and the bed before clicking, and carry a fire resistance potion. Ancient debris never generates exposed to air, so ignore open cave walls and mine solid netherrack instead.

name: Subspace Bubble
desc: Use the Nether to travel 7 km in the Overworld
howToGet: Understand the trick: the Nether compresses distance 8:1, so 1 block traveled there equals 8 blocks in the Overworld.
The advancement checks that your two Overworld portals are at least 7,000 blocks apart horizontally, which means 875 blocks in the Nether.
Enter your first portal, travel at least 875 blocks through the Nether (bring blocks, food and armor), and build a second portal there.
Step through. Landing at the far Overworld point completes the advancement and pays 100 XP.
tips: Tunnel through netherrack at a safe height instead of crossing open lava lakes, and mark your route. If the exit portal links back to an old one, move it further: the check is pure horizontal distance between your two Overworld points.

name: A Terrible Fortress
desc: Break your way into a Nether Fortress
howToGet: Enter the Nether through a lit portal, geared up: iron armor or better, a bow, food and a stack of blocks for bridging over lava.

Explore until you spot the dark red nether brick structure. Fortresses can generate in every Nether biome: the game splits the Nether into 432x432-block regions (480x480 in Bedrock) and each region rolls either one fortress or one bastion remnant, never both.

If a region gave you a bastion instead, keep moving: in Java each region has a 40% chance of a fortress (33% in Bedrock). In basalt deltas any structure attempt becomes a fortress, so fortresses are most common there.
Walk into the fortress itself. Just stepping inside completes the advancement.
tips: Fortresses can generate buried in netherrack with only a bridge or a tower sticking out, so scan the terrain edges. Don't confuse them with bastions: bastions are black blackstone, fortresses are dark red nether brick. A fire resistance potion makes the search far safer.

name: Who is Cutting Onions?
desc: Obtain Crying Obsidian
howToGet: Crying obsidian is the purple-glowing obsidian variant. There are two ways to get it.
Barter with piglins: throw gold ingots at adult piglins and each barter has about an 8.5% chance to return 1-3 crying obsidian.
Or find it: ruined portals generate with crying obsidian blocks, and their chests (and bastion remnant chests) can hold it.
Mine it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe and pick it up. Having it in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: Crying obsidian can't build a nether portal. Save 6 blocks for a respawn anchor, its main use, and the next step in this chain: charging one completes Not Quite "Nine" Lives.

name: Oh Shiny
desc: Distract Piglins with gold
howToGet: Take off any gold armor you are wearing: the advancement only triggers if you are NOT wearing golden armor (with gold on, piglins never turn hostile to you).
Make a piglin aggressive: punch it, mine gold ore or gilded blackstone near it, or open a chest in its sight.
Throw any gold item at the angry piglin. A gold ingot is the cheapest option.
The piglin stops attacking to pick up and examine the gold. That distraction completes the advancement.
tips: Any gold item works for the distraction, but only gold ingots trigger actual bartering with item returns. Keep an escape route ready: other piglins nearby stay hostile even while one admires your gold.

name: This Boat Has Legs
desc: Ride a Strider with a Warped Fungus on a Stick
howToGet: Craft a warped fungus on a stick: a fishing rod plus a warped fungus, which grows in warped forests or from bonemealing warped nylium.
Find a strider: the two-legged mobs that walk on lava lakes all over the Nether.
Saddle it. Saddles come from structure chests (nether fortresses, bastions, ancient cities), from fishing treasure, or from master leatherworker villagers.
Mount the saddled strider, hold the fungus on a stick and use it to boost. Riding it while the stick loses durability completes the advancement.
tips: Striders walk much faster on lava than on land, and they shiver and slow down when they leave it. Keep the ride on the lava lake and bring a spare fungus on a stick for long trips.

name: Uneasy Alliance
desc: Rescue a Ghast from the Nether, bring it safely home to the Overworld... and then kill it
howToGet: Find a Ghast in an open Nether area (soul sand valleys and basalt deltas have the most spawns) and note where it hovers.
Build a large nether portal nearby, at least 10x10 on the inside, so the 4-block-wide Ghast fits through comfortably. Light it.
Lure the Ghast through the portal: stand on the other side so it drifts toward you, and use a fishing rod to pull it the last blocks through the frame. Its fireballs cannot damage the obsidian frame.
Once it is through, go to the Overworld side yourself and kill it there. The advancement only requires that you are in the Overworld when you get the kill credit.
tips: Ghasts have only 10 health, so a single good bow shot usually finishes them. Build a cobblestone shelter on the Overworld side before starting: a fireball from your confused passenger can start fires everywhere. Return to Sender (killing a Ghast with its own fireball) is a natural warm-up for this one.

name: War Pigs
desc: Loot a Chest in a Bastion Remnant
howToGet: Find a Bastion Remnant in the Nether (any biome except Basalt Deltas) while wearing a piece of gold armor.
Locate a chest that generated naturally inside the bastion. Bridges and housing units have exposed chests; the treasure room chests sit under the lava.
Opening or breaking chests (and mining gold) angers nearby Piglins even if you wear gold. Clear them first, or pillar up out of reach.
Open the chest: the advancement triggers on the first chest opened in a bastion.
tips: The safe classic: break the blocks under a chest and place a hopper feeding into another chest below, then loot without ever opening it. Piglin Brutes do not care about your gold armor, so kill or block them off before looting the treasure room.

name: Cover Me in Debris
desc: Get a full suit of Netherite armor
howToGet: Wear a full suit of netherite armor: helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots, all at once.
That means 4 netherite ingots = 16 ancient debris + 16 gold ingots, plus 4 netherite upgrade smithing templates.

Find netherite upgrade templates in bastion remnant chests - see our bastion guide for loot routes. Duplicate each template at a crafting table with 7 diamonds + 1 netherrack + the template, so one find is enough.
Mine the ancient debris at Y=15 (beds or TNT), smelt to scrap, combine 4 scrap + 4 gold per ingot.
Upgrade diamond armor at a smithing table: diamond piece + template + netherite ingot. Put the four pieces on and the challenge completes - worth 100 XP.
tips: Upgrade armor you already enchanted: the smithing table keeps all enchantments, so there is no reason to make fresh diamond gear. If templates are your bottleneck, raid treasure bastions (the ones with the gold-block core) - they have the best chest loot.

name: Spooky Scary Skeleton
desc: Obtain a Wither Skeleton's skull
howToGet: Find a nether fortress (see the A Terrible Fortress guide): wither skeletons spawn only inside fortresses.
Kill wither skeletons. The skull drop chance is 2.5% by default, rising to 3.5%, 4.5% and 5.5% with Looting I, II and III (same on Java and Bedrock).
Only kills by you or a tamed wolf can drop the skull, so finish them yourself.
Pick the skull up: having it in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: A Looting III sword cuts the average from about 40 kills per skull to about 18, so enchant before farming. Watch the Wither effect: it drains your health and turns the hearts black; milk cures it. You need three skulls to summon the wither.

name: Into Fire
desc: Relieve a Blaze of its rod
howToGet: Find a nether fortress first (see the A Terrible Fortress guide): blazes spawn only in fortresses, both from the blaze monster spawners and throughout the structure.
Gear up for the fight: a fire resistance potion (from piglin bartering) makes blazes almost harmless.
Kill a blaze and make it drop a blaze rod: each blaze drops 0-1 rods, and only if the killing blow comes from you or a tamed wolf.
Pick the rod up. Having it in your inventory completes the advancement.
tips: A Looting III sword raises the drop to up to 4 rods per blaze, and snowballs hurt blazes. Take several rods home: blaze powder fuels brewing stands and crafts into eyes of ender.

name: Not Quite "Nine" Lives
desc: Charge a Respawn Anchor to the maximum

name: Feels Like Home
desc: Take a Strider for a loooong ride on a lava lake in the Overworld
howToGet: Bring a strider to the Overworld: lead it through your nether portal (a lead works, and they follow warped fungus).
Find an overworld lava lake: big surface lakes generate in some biomes, and there are lava aquifers in deep caves. A long lava river also works.
Ride the strider on the overworld lava for 50 blocks.
Only horizontal displacement counts, so riding in circles doesn't work: cover 50 blocks of real distance and the advancement pops.
tips: Pick a straight, wide lake and ride it end to end. Striders shiver and slow down off lava, so plan a route that stays on the molten stuff the whole way.

name: Hot Tourist Destinations
desc: Explore all Nether biomes
howToGet: Visit all 5 Nether biomes: nether wastes, crimson forest, warped forest, soul sand valley and basalt deltas. Only entering the biome counts - you do not need to do anything inside it.
Find your starting biome, then pick a direction and travel. Nether biomes are large but all five usually generate within a few hundred blocks of spawn.
Warped forest and basalt deltas are often the missing ones. If you cannot find one, travel 500+ blocks in a fresh direction before giving up.
Use the F3 debug screen to read the biome name as you cross borders.
Bring fire resistance, a shield, and blocks for bridging over lava lakes - basalt deltas in particular love vertical lava drops.
tips: The challenge pays 500 XP, so it is worth doing early. Biomes outside the Nether do not count, and there is no distance requirement inside each biome - stepping one block in is enough.

name: Withering Heights
desc: Summon the Wither
howToGet: Collect 4 blocks of Soul Sand or Soul Soil (soul sand valleys in the Nether) and 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls.
Farm the skulls at a Nether fortress: Wither Skeletons drop a skull 2.5% of the time, up to 5.5% with a Looting III sword.

Spawn the Wither in a controlled spot: place the soul sand in a T shape, then the 3 skulls on top. The safest options are far from your base in the open, or trapped under the bedrock ceiling of the Nether roof or the End's exit portal.
The advancement triggers as soon as the Wither finishes its spawn animation: you do not have to kill it for this one.
tips: If you fight it fairly, use a bow for the first half (it flies) and a Smite V sword for the second half, and carry milk buckets against the Wither effect. The bedrock trap method makes the whole fight risk-free and is the standard way to farm nether stars.

name: Local Brewery
desc: Brew a Potion
howToGet: Craft a brewing stand with 1 blaze rod and 3 blocks of any cobblestone-tier stone: cobblestone, blackstone and cobbled deepslate all work.
Or skip the crafting: brewing stands also generate in igloo basements and in village churches.
Fuel it with blaze powder and put water bottles in the three bottom slots (nether wart on top if you want real potions).
Take any item OUT of a potion slot: even a plain water bottle or an empty glass bottle counts. Picking it up completes the advancement.
tips: You don't need nether wart or a finished potion at all: loading water bottles and removing one already grants the advancement. An early village church is the fastest free brewing stand.

name: Bring Home the Beacon
desc: Construct and place a Beacon
howToGet: Defeat the wither to get a nether star (see the Withering Heights guide for the fight).
Craft the beacon: 5 glass, 3 obsidian and 1 nether star.

Build a pyramid of mineral blocks: iron, gold, diamond, emerald or netherite blocks, in any mix. A single 3x3 layer (9 blocks) powers a level-1 beacon; four full layers (164 blocks) unlock every effect.
Place the beacon on top, centered, with a clear view of the sky. When it powers on, stand within about 20 blocks of it (a 20x20x14 box) and the advancement triggers.
tips: Iron is the cheapest pyramid material by far, so mine or build an iron farm before committing diamond blocks. The beacon needs open sky above it: bedrock and most transparent blocks are fine, but solid blocks switch it off.

name: A Furious Cocktail
desc: Have every potion effect applied at the same time
howToGet: You need all 17 potion-obtainable status effects active at once: Fire Resistance, Infested, Invisibility, Jump Boost, Night Vision, Oozing, Poison, Regeneration, Resistance, Slow Falling, Slowness, Speed, Strength, Water Breathing, Weakness, Weaving and Wind Charged.

Brew every required potion: the 13 classic ones plus the four added in 1.21 (Wind Charging, Weaving, Oozing and Infestation, from Trial Chambers materials). A Potion of the Turtle Master covers Resistance and Slowness with one bottle.
Turn them into Splash Potions with gunpowder, stand still, and throw them at your feet in quick succession.
Throw the shortest-duration effects last (the Turtle Master is only 20 seconds at level I, so it goes last).
tips: Splash potions of extended duration make this much more forgiving. The source of the effect does not matter, so tipped arrows shot straight up or a beacon's Regeneration also count. The 100 XP reward makes it a decent burst of experience late-game.

name: Beaconator
desc: Bring a Beacon to full power
howToGet: Kill the Wither to get a Nether Star (see the Withering Heights guide).
Craft a Beacon: 5 Glass, 3 Obsidian and the Nether Star.
Gather 164 mineral blocks for a full pyramid: 81 (9x9) + 49 (7x7) + 25 (5x5) + 9 (3x3). Iron, gold, diamond, emerald and netherite blocks all count and can be mixed. Iron is cheapest: 1,476 ingots.
Stack the four layers with the beacon on top, feed it an ingot or gem, and select a primary power.
tips: A full 4-layer pyramid unlocks the secondary power (Regeneration or a level II effect). You can share one pyramid between up to 6 beacons by placing them in a 3x2 arrangement on top, which is the standard endgame base setup.

name: How Did We Get Here?
desc: Have every effect applied at the same time
howToGet: This hidden challenge needs all 27 status effects at the same time. Build the classic machine: a water column or bubble elevator with an elder guardian nearby (Mining Fatigue), a shulker trap (Levitation), and a dolphin tank (Dolphin's Grace).

Stock up first: potions and splash potions for every effect, a turtle master potion, suspicious stews for the flower effects, a totem, golden apples, a conduit setup, a beacon, honey blocks, and a raid for Bad Omen into Hero of the Village.
Kill a raid captain for Bad Omen, then trigger and win a raid so it converts into Hero of the Village.
Set everything up in one spot and apply the effects in order of duration: longest first (conduit, beacon, elder guardian), shortest last (shulker levitation, dolphin, turtle master).
Get hit by the shulker, swim past the dolphin, drink the remaining potions, eat the gapple, and the advancement pops the moment the 27th effect lands.
tips: Watch a video guide once before building - the exact station layout matters. Most players fail on the timing window of Dolphin's Grace and Levitation, so practice the last 10 seconds of the sequence. The advancement is hidden: it only appears in the tab after you earn it.
searchNote: How to get How Did We Get Here, all 27 effects list, hidden challenge

name: The End
desc: Or the beginning?

name: Free the End
desc: Good luck
howToGet: Find a stronghold with eyes of ender (throw them and follow - see our stronghold guide), fill the portal frame and enter.
Destroy the end crystals on top of the obsidian pillars first: shoot the exposed ones with a bow, and pillar up or shoot through the iron bars of the two caged ones.

Then fight the dragon: shoot it while it flies, and attack the head when it perches on the bedrock fountain. Beds explode in the End and deal massive damage to the perched dragon if you want the speedrun method.
Bring: carved pumpkin or keep your crosshair low (endermen), a water bucket for falls and endermen, slow falling potions if you have them, food, and your best bow and sword.
When the dragon dies the advancement unlocks, the exit portal opens, and the dragon egg appears on top.
tips: Do not look at the void while bridging - build the pillar-to-cage climbs with blocks you do not mind losing, and put your respawn point on a bed in the stronghold before entering. The egg teleports when punched: place a torch under it and break the block it sits on.

name: The Next Generation
desc: Hold the Dragon Egg
howToGet: Defeat the Ender Dragon (see the Free the End guide). The Dragon Egg appears on top of the exit portal fountain.
Do not left-click the egg directly: it teleports up to 15 blocks away and can fall into the portal, where it is lost.
Instead, dig under the block below the egg, place a torch there and break the block the egg sits on. It falls onto the torch and drops as an item. A piston push works too.
Pick it up: the advancement triggers when the egg enters your inventory.
tips: Only one egg exists per world, so treat it as the rarest trophy in the game. Keep it in an ender chest or item frame, not in a chest somewhere you will forget.

name: Remote Getaway
desc: Escape the island

name: The End... Again...
desc: Respawn the Ender Dragon
howToGet: Kill the ender dragon once first (see the Free the End guide).
Craft 4 end crystals: each one takes 7 glass, 1 eye of ender and 1 ghast tear.
Go to the exit portal, the bedrock fountain at the center of the End.
Place one end crystal on the middle of each of the portal's 4 sides.
The crystals rebuild the tower crystals and summon a new dragon. Stay within about 192 blocks of the portal center and the advancement is yours.
tips: Respawned dragons drop 500 XP instead of the original 12,000, but each kill (up to 20) generates a new end gateway, the fastest way to the outer End islands without bridging.

name: You Need a Mint
desc: Collect Dragon's Breath in a Glass Bottle
howToGet: Bring a stack of empty Glass Bottles to the End (craft from glass, or buy from cleric villagers).
During the dragon fight, watch for the Ender Dragon's breath attack: it leaves a purple lingering cloud on the ground. Its fireballs leave the same clouds on impact.
Right-click the purple cloud with an empty bottle to collect Dragon's Breath.
tips: Dragon's Breath is the ingredient for Lingering Potions (brew it with a splash potion), which are required for tipped arrows. Collect at least a dozen while you are there: coming back later means respawning the dragon.

name: The City at the End of the Game
desc: Go on in, what could happen?
howToGet: Defeat the Ender Dragon. A bedrock-framed End Gateway portal spawns floating above the outer rim (up to 20 gateways as you kill more dragons).
Throw an Ender Pearl into the gateway's center to teleport to the outer End islands. (Entering with a trapdoor crawl or by flying in also works.)
Explore the outer islands until you spot an End City: tall purpur towers with End Rods on top.
Walk inside the city: the advancement triggers on entering its bounding box.
tips: Bring several stacks of blocks, extra Ender Pearls and slow-falling options before pearl-ing through: the outer islands have huge void gaps. Cities with a floating End Ship next to them are the ones that hold Elytra (see the Sky's the Limit guide).

name: Sky's the Limit
desc: Find Elytra
parent: The City at the End of the Game
howToGet: Kill the ender dragon first, then throw an ender pearl through the small bedrock gateway that appears (aim carefully - it is one block high).
You land in the outer End. Travel outward, bridging or ender-pearling between islands, until you spot an end city - they are tall purpur towers visible from far away.
Only some end cities have an end ship floating next to them. That ship is what you need.
Fight or dodge the shulkers (their levitation bullets make you float - eat chorus fruit or place water to land safely), climb the ship, and take the elytra from the item frame in the hull.
Grab the dragon head on the ship's bow and the loot chests while you are there.
tips: Bring plenty of blocks, slow falling potions, and an ender chest with backup gear - dying in the outer End without a linked ender chest means starting the bridge-walk over. Elytra can be repaired with phantom membranes at an anvil, so do not let it break.

name: Great View From Up Here
desc: Levitate up 50 blocks from the attacks of a Shulker
parent: The City at the End of the Game
howToGet: Defeat the ender dragon and use an end gateway to reach an end city.
Let a shulker bullet hit you: it applies Levitation for 10 seconds.
Travel 50 blocks vertically while Levitation is active. The distance counts in either direction and doesn't have to be caused by the levitation itself.
Easiest method: stand at the bottom of a tall end city tower, get hit and float up the open shaft; extra hits from other shulkers keep you rising.
The advancement (and 50 XP) triggers the instant your vertical travel with Levitation reaches 50 blocks.
tips: The real danger is the landing: when the effect ends you fall. Carry a water bucket, ender pearls or slow falling potions, and never drink milk mid-air, since milk removes the Levitation keeping you up.

name: Adventure
desc: Adventure, exploration and combat

name: Heart Transplanter
desc: Place a Creaking Heart with the correct alignment between two Pale Oak Log blocks
howToGet: Find a pale garden at night and locate an active creaking heart tucked between two pale oak logs.
Mine it with a Silk Touch tool: without Silk Touch the heart breaks and drops nothing.
Take 2 pale oak logs from the same forest.
Rebuild the sandwich anywhere: two pale oak logs with the creaking heart directly between them along the same axis.
Placing it with the correct alignment completes the advancement.
tips: Silk Touch is mandatory, so enchant an axe before visiting the pale garden. A correctly placed heart behaves like a natural one: it activates at night and can spawn creakings, so place your transplant far from your base.

name: Voluntary Exile
desc: Kill a raid captain. Maybe consider staying away from villages for the time being...
howToGet: Find a raid captain: either a Pillager patrol (they wander the Overworld after a few in-game days) or the captains stationed at a Pillager Outpost. Captains wear an ominous banner on their head.
Kill the captain. The advancement is hidden, so it pops up as a surprise the moment you do it.
Since 1.21, captains drop an Ominous Bottle instead of cursing you directly: drinking it applies Bad Omen, which starts a raid when you enter a village.
tips: This is the first half of the raid loop: keep the Ominous Bottle, find a village and drink it there to trigger a raid, then win it for Hero of the Village. Until you are ready for that, heed the warning in the description and keep your distance from villages after the kill if a patrol surprise-attacked you mid-errand.

name: Country Lode, Take Me Home
desc: Use a Compass on a Lodestone

name: Is It a Bird?
desc: Look at a Parrot through a Spyglass

name: Monster Hunter
desc: Kill any hostile monster

name: The Power of Books
desc: Read the power signal of a Chiseled Bookshelf using a Comparator

name: What a Deal!
desc: Successfully trade with a Villager
howToGet: Find any villager in a village, or a wandering trader with its llamas.
Right-click it to open the trade window and check what it wants: usually emeralds, or items for emeralds.
Place the cost in the input slot.
Take the item out of the trading output slot. Grabbing the result completes the advancement.
tips: Novice villagers offer the cheapest trades, and curing a zombie villager (see the Zombie Doctor guide) drops prices massively. Wandering trader trades count too, and trading is the only way to get some items like explorer maps.

name: Crafting a New Look
desc: Craft a trimmed armor at a Smithing Table

name: Sticky Situation
desc: Jump into a Honey Block to break your fall
howToGet: Get a honey block: fill glass bottles at a full bee nest or beehive (honey level 5) and craft 4 honey bottles into one. A campfire under the nest keeps the bees calm while you harvest.
Place the honey block high up with open air beside it: on the side of a pillar or a cliff.
Jump from above and fall PAST the block, hugging its vertical side. Landing on top doesn't count: you must collide with the side while falling.
The block slows you into a slide down its face, and that completes the advancement.
tips: Easiest setup: build a 10-block pillar, stick one honey block on its side near the top, climb up, walk off and drift into the wall. The honey slide also removes all fall damage from that slide.

name: Ol' Betsy
desc: Shoot a Crossbow
howToGet: Get a crossbow: craft one with 3 sticks, 2 string, 1 iron ingot and 1 tripwire hook, loot one from pillager outpost or bastion chests, or take it from a pillager or crossbow piglin that drops it.
Carry arrows (or firework rockets) anywhere in your inventory.
Hold use to load the crossbow: it stays loaded until you fire.
Press use again to shoot. Your first shot completes the advancement.
tips: Quick Charge III makes reloading almost instant and Multishot fires three projectiles at once; both enchantments are crossbow-only. Loading firework rockets turns the crossbow into a small grenade launcher with area damage.

name: Surge Protector
desc: Protect a Villager from an undesired shock without starting a fire

name: Caves & Cliffs
desc: Free fall from the top of the world (build limit) to the bottom of the world and survive
howToGet: The requirement: free fall from at least Y=319 down to at most Y=-59, more than 379 blocks, and survive.
Find the spot: a tall mountain with a deep cave system under it is ideal. Dig or find a shaft from the summit down to the deepslate layers.
Prepare the landing: a pool of water, a slime block or powder snow at the bottom (below Y=-59) cancels fall damage.
Stand at the top at Y=319 or higher and WALK off the edge. Don't jump first: jumping before the fall tends to not award the advancement.
Survive the landing below Y=-59 and the advancement completes.
tips: A water bucket placed at the bottom is the classic safe landing, and carrying a second one mid-fall is good insurance. Check your Y coordinates with the F3 debug screen so both ends of the drop count.

name: Respecting the Remnants
desc: Brush a Suspicious block to obtain a Pottery Sherd

name: Sneak 100
desc: Sneak near a Sculk Sensor or Warden to prevent it from detecting you

name: Sweet Dreams
desc: Sleep in a Bed to change your respawn point
howToGet: Craft a bed: 3 wool of the same color on top of 3 planks of any wood.
Place it anywhere with room and right-click it at night (or during a thunderstorm).
The advancement triggers the instant you are IN the bed: you don't even need to fall asleep.
Sleeping also sets your respawn point to the bed.
tips: Never right-click a bed in the Nether or the End: it explodes. If you want to sleep on a trip without moving your spawn point, the straw bed from 26.3 is single-use and leaves your spawn untouched.

name: Hero of the Village
desc: Successfully defend a village from a raid
howToGet: Kill a raid captain (the pillager with the ominous banner on its head, found in patrols or at pillager outposts) to get Bad Omen.
Walk into a village with Bad Omen active - the raid starts immediately. In current versions you drink the ominous bottle instead: the effect no longer applies on kill.
Defend the village: the raid has 3 waves (Easy), 5 (Normal) or 7 (Hard), scaling with difficulty. Ring the bell to highlight raiders through walls.
Kill at least one raider yourself - the advancement requires your participation, not just an iron golem doing the work.
Survive until the victory message: you get Hero of the Village (hidden advancement), big trading discounts from every villager, and gifts thrown at you.
tips: Walling the village first trivializes most waves - raiders pathfind to beds and villagers. Bring a totem for vindicators and evokers on Hard, and watch for witches healing the raiders in later waves.

name: Is It a Balloon?
desc: Look at a Ghast through a Spyglass

name: A Throwaway Joke
desc: Throw a Trident at something. Note: Throwing away your only weapon is not a good idea.

name: It Spreads
desc: Kill a mob near a Sculk Catalyst

name: Take Aim
desc: Shoot something with an Arrow

name: Monsters Hunted
desc: Kill one of every hostile monster
howToGet: Kill one of each of the 41 hostile monsters on the advancement's list, from common Zombies and Creepers to the Ender Dragon, the Wither, the Elder Guardian, the Warden and newer mobs like the Breeze, the Bogged, the Creaking (kill it by destroying its creaking heart) and the Parched.

Work through it systematically: Overworld night mobs first (Zombie, Skeleton, Creeper, Spider, Enderman, Witch, Slime, Phantom, Husk, Stray, Drowned, Silverfish, Cave Spider, Endermite, Zombie Villager...).
Then the Nether set: Blaze, Ghast, Magma Cube, Wither Skeleton, Hoglin, Zoglin, Piglin, Piglin Brute and Zombified Piglin.

Finish with the structure and boss mobs: Guardian and Elder Guardian (ocean monument), Shulker (End city), Evoker, Vindicator, Vex, Ravager and Pillager (mansion and raids), Breeze (trial chambers), Warden (deep dark), Ender Dragon and Wither.
tips: Your advancement screen tracks which ones are still missing, so check it after each expedition. The Warden is the scariest entry: bring wool to sneak on, or kill it with a bow from a pillar outside its reach. Note that killing a Creaking only counts if you destroy its creaking heart, not by hitting the mob itself.

name: Postmortal
desc: Use a Totem of Undying to cheat death
howToGet: Get a Totem of Undying: Evokers drop one every time. Find them in a Woodland Mansion, or in raid waves 5+ at a village.
Hold the totem in your main hand or off-hand.
Take fatal damage with the totem equipped: instead of dying, you get restored with Absorption, Regeneration and Fire Resistance, and the advancement triggers.
tips: The safest way to trigger it on purpose is jumping off a tall pillar with the totem in hand. The totem does not save you from the void or from /kill, so it cannot help with Elytra accidents in the End void.

name: Mob Kabob
desc: Hit five mobs in the same Charge attack using the Spear.

name: Hired Help
desc: Summon an Iron Golem to help defend a village
howToGet: Gather 36 iron ingots and craft them into 4 iron blocks.
Build the body: one iron block on the ground, then three more across the top in a T shape.
Carve a pumpkin with shears (or use a jack o'lantern) and place it on top of the center block LAST.
The iron golem comes to life instantly, and the advancement triggers.
tips: The pumpkin must go on last: placing it before the body does nothing. A golem you build yourself never attacks you, unlike village golems defending their villagers. Iron farms abuse exactly this recipe.

name: Star Trader
desc: Trade with a Villager at the build height limit

name: Smithing with Style
desc: Apply these smithing templates at least once: Spire, Snout, Rib, Ward, Silence, Vex, Tide, Wayfinder

name: Two Birds, One Arrow
desc: Kill two Phantoms with a piercing Arrow

name: Who's the Pillager Now?
desc: Give a Pillager a taste of their own medicine

name: Arbalistic
desc: Kill five unique mobs with one crossbow shot

name: Careful Restoration
desc: Make a Decorated Pot out of 4 Pottery Sherds

name: Adventuring Time
desc: Discover every biome
howToGet: Visit all 56 biomes in the advancement's list. The counter only counts biomes you physically stand in, and it is per-world per-player.
Cover your home continent first on foot or horseback: most temperate biomes (forests, plains, rivers, beaches, mountains) sit within a few thousand blocks of spawn.
Use an Elytra with fireworks for the long haul: oceans (cold, frozen, lukewarm, deep variants), mushroom fields, and the far climates are much faster by air.
Do not forget the cave biomes (Dripstone Caves, Lush Caves, Deep Dark) and the vertical mountain biomes (Jagged Peaks, Frozen Peaks, Stony Peaks, Grove, Meadow, Cherry Grove).
tips: The F3 debug screen shows your current biome, and the advancement's progress list shows which ones remain. At 500 XP this is the single biggest experience reward of any advancement, so save the last biome for when you need the levels.

name: Sound of Music
desc: Make the Meadows come alive with the sound of music from a Jukebox

name: Light as a Rabbit
desc: Walk on Powder Snow... without sinking in it

name: Is It a Plane?
desc: Look at the Ender Dragon through a Spyglass

name: Very Very Frightening
desc: Strike a Villager with lightning
howToGet: Get a Trident: Drowned occasionally spawn holding one and drop it (about 8.5% chance, higher with Looting).
Enchant it with Channeling (enchanting table, librarian trade or looted books).
Wait for a thunderstorm (a real storm, not just rain).
Hit a Villager with the thrown trident during the storm: lightning strikes it, the villager turns into a Witch, and the advancement triggers.
tips: Do this away from your trading hall, since lightning also kills livestock and can turn pigs into zombified piglins. The same Channeling trident on a Creeper creates a Charged Creeper, which is how you farm mob heads.

name: Sniper Duel
desc: Kill a Skeleton from at least 50 meters away
howToGet: Kill a skeleton with an arrow from at least 50 blocks away - horizontal distance is what counts.
Easiest setup: pillar up at night or find a skeleton trapped in a two-block hole, mark its position, walk 50+ blocks back, and shoot.
Arrows drop over distance, so aim noticeably above the skeleton's head. A Power-enchanted bow makes the kill one or two shots.
Alternative cheese: put a skeleton in a boat or minecart, back off 50 blocks, and it cannot dodge.
The kill must be with the arrow itself - the bow's punch or fire ticks after impact still count as long as the arrow dealt the damage.
tips: Do it in a flat area at dawn with a name-tagged skeleton you prepared the night before. Deserts and frozen rivers give clean 50-block sightlines without trees in the way.

name: Bullseye
desc: Hit the bullseye of a Target block from at least 30 meters away
howToGet: Craft a Target block: 4 Redstone dust around 1 Hay Bale.
Place it with a clear line of sight and mark a shooting spot at least 30 blocks away (use F3 coordinates to be sure).
Shoot an arrow (or throw a trident) into the red bullseye center from that spot. A redstone lamp behind the target lights up for 4 redstone ticks on a perfect hit, confirming your aim.
tips: The hard part is the arrow arc over 30+ blocks: aim well above the target. Crossbows work too, and a multishot crossbow triples your chances per shot. Once the mechanics click, this also doubles as target practice for Sniper Duel.

name: Isn't It Scute?
desc: Get Armadillo Scutes from an Armadillo using a Brush

name: Minecraft: Trial(s) Edition
desc: Step foot in a Trial Chamber

name: Crafters Crafting Crafters
desc: Be near a Crafter when it crafts a Crafter

desc: Scrape a Copper Bulb with an Axe to make it brighter

name: Who Needs Rockets?
desc: Use a Wind Charge to launch yourself upwards 8 blocks

desc: Unlock a Vault with a Trial Key

desc: Unlock an Ominous Vault with an Ominous Trial Key

desc: Kill a Breeze with a deflected Breeze-shot Wind Charge

desc: Deal 50 hearts of damage in a single hit using the Mace

name: Husbandry
desc: The world is full of friends and food

name: Stay Hydrated!
desc: Place a Dried Ghast block into water

name: Bee Our Guest
desc: Use a Campfire to collect Honey from a Beehive using a Glass Bottle without aggravating the Bees
howToGet: Find a bee nest on an oak or birch tree near flowers (meadow trees almost always have one), or craft a beehive from 6 planks and 3 honeycombs.
Wait for honey level 5: honey visibly drips from the nest.
Place a campfire directly under the nest, within 5 blocks and with no blocks in between: the smoke keeps the bees calm.
Use a glass bottle on the nest to collect a honey bottle without angering anyone. That calm harvest completes the advancement.
tips: A dispenser loaded with glass bottles can harvest honey without ever angering the bees, no campfire needed. And a Silk Touch tool moves a whole nest with its bees inside (see the Total Beelocation guide).

name: The Parrots and the Bats
desc: Breed two animals together

name: You've Got a Friend in Me
desc: Have an Allay deliver items to you

name: Whatever Floats Your Goat!
desc: Get in a Boat and float with a Goat

name: Best Friends Forever
desc: Tame an animal
howToGet: Pick a tameable animal: Wolf (bones), Cat (raw cod or salmon), Parrot (any seeds), Horse, Donkey, Mule or Llama (repeated riding), among others.
For a wolf: collect bones from skeletons, find one in a taiga or forest, and feed bones until hearts appear and it gets a red collar.
For horses and llamas: right-click to mount repeatedly until it stops bucking you off and shows hearts.
tips: A tamed wolf is the most useful first pet: it fights beside you and teleports to you. Tame several and you have a small army for the Monsters Hunted grind.

name: Glow and Behold!
desc: Make the text of any kind of sign glow

name: Fishy Business
desc: Catch a fish

name: Total Beelocation
desc: Move a Bee Nest or Beehive, with 3 Bees inside, using Silk Touch

name: Bukkit Bukkit
desc: Catch a Tadpole in a Bucket

name: Uh Oh
desc: Have a Sulfur Cube absorb a TNT block

name: Smells Interesting
desc: Obtain a Sniffer Egg

name: A Seedy Place
desc: Plant a seed and watch it grow

name: Wax On
desc: Apply Honeycomb to a Copper block!

name: Two by Two
desc: Breed all the animals!
howToGet: Breed every breedable animal at least once - around 20 species including cows, sheep, pigs, chickens, wolves, cats, horses, donkeys, llamas, rabbits, turtles, axolotls, frogs, goats, camels, sniffers, armadillos and the rest. Mules do not count as separate (they come from horse + donkey), and yes, hoglins and striders count too.
Most overworld farm animals are straightforward: pen two of each and feed them their food.

The rare ones plan around: turtles (seagrass, beaches), sniffers (torchflower seeds from archaeology, then breed two sniffers), axolotls (tropical fish buckets, lush caves), frogs (slimeballs), hoglins (crimson fungi, they attack you), and pandas/foxes/polar bears variants.
Nether animals need to be bred in the Nether: hoglins and striders (warped fungi).
Keep a checklist - the advancement does not tell you which species you are missing.
tips: Start a breeding ranch near spawn and ship rare pairs home with leads and boats. Sniffers are the long pole: you need two eggs from brushing suspicious sand/gravel in warm ocean ruins and trail ruins, so check our archaeology guide.

name: Birthday Song
desc: Have an Allay drop a Cake at a Note Block
parent: You've Got a Friend in Me

name: A Complete Catalogue
desc: Tame all Cat variants!
howToGet: Tame all 11 cat variants: Tabby, Tuxedo, Red, Siamese, British Shorthair, Calico, Persian, Ragdoll, White, Jellie and Black.
Stray cats spawn in villages with at least one villager and four beds, so village-hopping is the core strategy. Each village cats spawn in random variants.
The Black cat is special: a guaranteed black cat spawns inside every Swamp Hut (witch hut), and black cats also spawn in villages during a full moon.
Tame them with Raw Cod or Raw Salmon: sneak, hold the fish, stand still and let the cat approach you, then feed it when it is close.
tips: Cats sprint away from players who move quickly, so patience matters more than fish count. Tamed cats follow you, can be told to sit, and occasionally bring you morning gifts when you sleep, including Phantom Membranes for Slow Falling potions.

name: Tactical Fishing
desc: Catch a Fish... without a Fishing Rod!
howToGet: Craft a bucket from 3 iron ingots and fill it with water anywhere.
Find a fish: cod, salmon, pufferfish or tropical fish in rivers and oceans.
Use the water bucket directly ON the fish, not on the water: aim at the fish itself.
The fish scoops straight into your bucket. The bucket of fish completes the advancement.
tips: A bucketed fish never despawns, making buckets the only way to move live fish: stock an aquarium, carry tropical fish to breed axolotls, or stash a pufferfish for a water breathing potion.

name: When the Squad Hops into Town
desc: Get each Frog variant on a Lead

name: Little Sniffs
desc: Feed a Snifflet

name: A Balanced Diet
desc: Eat everything that is edible, even if it's not good for you
howToGet: Eat each of the 40 foods on the advancement's list, from Apples, Bread and Steak to the weird ones: Rotten Flesh, Spider Eye, Poisonous Potato, Pufferfish, Suspicious Stew, Chorus Fruit, Glow Berries and a Honey Bottle.
Farm and cook the basics early: all raw and cooked meats, potatoes (raw, baked and poisonous), carrots, beetroot and its soup, bread, cookies, pumpkin pie and dried kelp.
Pick up the forage items on your travels: Sweet Berries (taiga), Glow Berries (lush caves), Melon Slices (jungle), Chorus Fruit (End cities) and Honey Bottles (bee nests).

Save the rarest for last: Enchanted Golden Apple (structure chests only), Golden Apple, Golden Carrot, Rabbit Stew, Mushroom Stew and Suspicious Stew (craft from flowers or buy from farmer villagers).
tips: Eating everything in one sitting is impossible since hunger limits you, so keep a dedicated chest of weird foods and snack between activities. Note the nasty effects: Pufferfish gives Poison and Hunger, and Suspicious Stew effects depend on the flower used. The advancement only requires eating, not surviving comfortably.

name: Serious Dedication
desc: Use a Netherite Ingot to upgrade a Hoe, and then reevaluate your life choices
howToGet: Craft or find a netherite upgrade smithing template (bastion remnants, duplicatable with 7 diamonds + netherrack).
Get one netherite ingot: 4 ancient debris smelted to scrap + 4 gold ingots.
Craft a diamond hoe - yes, a diamond hoe.
At a smithing table, combine diamond hoe + template + netherite ingot.
Enjoy your netherite hoe. The advancement is the game judging you.
tips: The real cost is one netherite ingot and two diamonds - trivial once you have a debris mining route. Do it after Cover Me in Debris, when one spare ingot means nothing.

desc: Team up with an axolotl and win a fight

desc: Tame one of each Wolf variant
